title: Session-proxy eviction and reroute strategy for active-active edge gateways
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In active-active hosted API deployments we observe a class of user-visible errors when a regional gateway needs to shed load or gracefully drain traffic. Streaming sessions (HTTP/2 or websockets) can be interrupted mid-response, and session-affine KV caches are lost when connections are rehomed.

Goal: Define and implement a session-proxy eviction + reroute strategy that preserves stream consistency where possible, minimizes tail latency during failovers, and integrates with existing circuit breaker/load-shedding policies. The strategy should be compatible with our smart routing layer, prefix/KV cache model, and existing canary/rollout mechanisms.

Scope: edge gateways (hosted API), regional failover orchestrator, session-proxy component(s), runtime hooks to checkpoint KV cache and streaming state, telemetry and SLOs for failover windows. Not in scope: on-prem private control plane changes (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming sessions that are actively producing tokens should experience either: seamless handoff (<=100ms continuity gap) or clean termination with clear error code and automatic client-side retry guidance.
- Non-streaming requests should be rerouted with <1s median additional latency in the common case.
- No increase in 99.9th percentile token-latency above the SLO for normal traffic during a controlled drain.
- System emits clear metrics for: evictions/sec, reroutes/sec, successful-kv-checkpoints, failed-checkpoints, circuit-trips, and P50/P95 reroute-latency.
- Integration test that simulates regional overload and validates behavior against above thresholds.
plan:
1) Design: finalize eviction policy and handshake protocol with session-proxy team (2d). 2) Implementation: session-proxy: checkpoint API, in-flight token forwarding, graceful drain hook (5d). 3) Orchestrator: failover coordinator enhancements to request checkpoints and coordinate short-lived sticky proxying (4d). 4) Runtime: accept lightweight resumable stream token envelope (3d). 5) Observability: dashboards + alerts (2d). 6) Staged rollout: internal dogfood -> canary -> 10% -> ramp (7d).

Implementation notes: use lightweight signed checkpoint blobs stored in regional S3 for fast lookup; coordinate with KV-cache eviction TTLs; on circuit-breaker open, prefer conservative checkpoint+terminate instead of aggressive blackhole.
notes:
Trade-offs considered: 
- Full state sync vs checkpoint-on-eviction: checkpoint-on-eviction chosen for latency/cost trade-off.
- Blocking handoff (synchronous) vs asynchronous resume token: asynchronous resume tokens reduce handoff latency at the cost of slightly more complex resume logic.
- Conservative reroute (hold traffic for 100ms) vs immediate reroute: selected hybrid where short hold is attempted and after threshold we reroute.

Open questions: 
- Should we encrypt checkpoint blobs with customer-specific KMS keys for private tenants? (security/ops decision).
- Impact on per-customer cost when checkpoint frequency increases.

Mitigations: back-pressure the checkpointing by sampling (<5% of sessions) for non-P0 customers, and prefer in-memory mirroring for Dedicated pools.

Key points: 1) region asks session-proxy to checkpoint; 2) proxy returns signed resume token; 3) orchestrator updates routing table; 4) new gateway uses token to resume KV context where possible. Posted design draft to Confluence.
